swallow: SWAL'LOW, noun A bird of the genus Hirundo, of many species, among which are the chimney swallow and the martin.

SWAL'LOW, noun [Saxon swalewe; Dutch zwaluw; German schwalbe; Danish svale; Swedish svala.] A bird of the genus Hirundo, of many species, among which are the chimney swallow and the martin. SWAL'LOW, verb transitive [Saxon swelgan, swilgan, to swallow, to swill; Dutch zwelgen; Swedish svälja, to swallow; svalg, the throat; Danish svælger. Query the French avaler, with a prefix, and the root of fall.] 1. To take into the stomach; to receive through the gullet or esophagus into the stomach; as, to swallow food or drink. Food should be well chewed before it is swallowed. 2. To absorb; to draw and sink into an abyss or gulf; to ingulf; usually followed by up. The earth opened and swallowed them up. Numbers 16. 3. To receive or embrace, as opinions or belief, without examination or scruple; to receive implicitly. 4. To engross; to appropriate. 5. To occupy; to employ. 6. To seize and waste. 7. To engross; to engage completely. The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink; they are swallowed up of wine. Isaiah 28. 8. To exhaust; to consume. His expenses swallow up all his income. SWAL'LOW, noun 1. The gullet or esophagus; the throat. 2. Voracity. 3. As much as is swallowed at once.
